Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:10:1.english: And permitted to derive benefit - As it is written (Exodus 22:30): “You shall cast it to the dogs.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:11:1.hebrew: שחוט שלי בשלי - שחוט זבחי בחצרי, כדכתיב (ויקרא א׳:ה׳) ושחט את בן הבקר וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:11:1.english: Slaughter Mine in Mine - Slaughter My sacrifices in My courtyard, as it is written (Leviticus 1:5): “And he shall slaughter the young bull [before the Lord]...”

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:11:2.hebrew: ושלך בשלך - כדכתיב (דברים י״ב:כ״א) וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך, וסיפיה דקרא — בשעריך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:11:2.english: And yours in your [place] - As it is written: “And you shall slaughter of your herd and of your flock” (Deuteronomy 12:21), and the end of the verse [states]: “in your gates.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:11:3.hebrew: מה שלי בשלך אסור - בהנאה, דמי יתיר הנאה שנאסר בה מחיים, אחרי שאין דמו נזרק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:11:3.english: Just as that which is Mine in yours is forbidden - [It is forbidden] from [deriving] benefit; for what will permit the benefit in which it was forbidden during [its] lifetime, since its blood is not sprinkled?

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:14:1.hebrew: ושחטו ושחט אותו ושחט אותו מה ת"ל - שלש פרשיות סמוכות זו לזו בשלמים: בראשונה כתיב ושחטו פתח אהל מועד, ובשתים כתיב ושחט אותו. מת"ל? אלו שלשה מיעוטין, דמשמע מכולהו: זה נשחט בעזרה, ולא אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:14:1.english: “And he shall slaughter it,” “and he shall slaughter it,” “and he shall slaughter it” — what does the verse teach? - [There are] three sections adjacent to one another regarding peace-offerings: In the first, it is written: “And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,” and in [the other] two, it is written: “And he shall slaughter it.” What does the verse teach? These are three exclusions, as it is implied from all of them: This is slaughtered in the Courtyard, and not another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:1.hebrew: לפי שנאמר כי ירחק וזבחת - ובא הכתוב להתיר להם בשר תאוה משיבאו לארץ והם יתרחקו מן המשכן, לפי שבמדבר לא הותרו לאכול שום בהמה הראויה להקרבה אלא על ידי הקרבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:1.english: Because it is stated: “If [the place] be too far... then you shall slaughter” - And the verse comes to permit them meat of desire once they enter the Land and are distanced from the Tabernacle, since in the wilderness they were not permitted to eat any animal fit for sacrifice except by means of an offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:2.english: At a distance from the place - Outside the Temple.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:3.hebrew: אתה זובח - חולין שלך, ואי אתה זובח בעזרה, שהוא מקום הקרוב לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:3.english: You may slaughter - Your non-sacred [animals]; but you may not slaughter in the [Temple] Courtyard, which is the place close to it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:4.hebrew: ה"ג - פרט לחולין, שלא ישחטו בעזרה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:15:4.english: This is the reading - “Excluding non-sacred [animals], that they should not be slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:1.hebrew: אלא תמימים - ובראויה להקרבה הכתוב מדבר, דאילו בשאין ראויה להקרבה, לא איתסר בשר תאוה דידהו במדבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:1.english: Only unblemished - And the verse speaks of [an animal that is] fit for sacrifice, for regarding [animals] that are not fit for sacrifice, their meat of desire [i.e., non-sacred meat] was not forbidden in the wilderness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:2.hebrew: שכן מין הכשר - להקריב. כיון דדמי להו בהכי, אתי למיגמר ליה במה מצינו, להחמיר ולאסור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:2.english: Since [they are of] the fit type - To be sacrificed. Since it is similar to them in this [regard], it comes to be derived from it via a mah matzinu [analogy], to be stringent and to prohibit [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:3.hebrew: שהיא בשחיטה כבהמה - ואיתקש לפסולי המוקדשין בפרשה זאת: "אך כאשר יאכל את הצבי וגו'". ודרשינן ליה בשחיטת חולין (דף כח.): מה פסולי המוקדשין בשחיטה — אף צבי ואיל בשחיטה. וכיון דבשחיטה איתקש להו, איכא למיגמר נמי מינה שלא תהא שחיטה בעזרה, דכל דבר זביחה אסר רחמנא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:3.english: Since it is [rendered fit] by slaughter like a domesticated animal - And it is juxtaposed with disqualified consecrated animals in this passage: “Only as the gazelle is eaten, etc.” And we expound it in [tractate] Shechitat Chullin (28a): Just as disqualified consecrated animals [require] slaughter, so too a gazelle and a deer [require] slaughter. And since it was juxtaposed with them regarding slaughter, it can also be derived from this that [its] slaughter must not take place in the [Temple] courtyard, for the Merciful One prohibited anything [subject to] slaughter [from being slaughtered in the courtyard].

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:4.hebrew: ושחטו ושחט אותו ושחט אותו מה ת"ל - שלש פרשיות סמוכות זו לזו בשלמים: בראשונה כתיב "ושחטו פתח אהל מועד", ובשתים כתיב "ושחט אותו". מת"ל? אלו שלשה מיעוטין, דמשמע מכולהו: זה נשחט בעזרה, ולא אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:4.english: “And he shall slaughter it,” “and he shall slaughter it,” “and he shall slaughter it” — what does the verse teach? - [There are] three sections adjacent to one another in [the passage of] peace offerings: In the first, it is written, “And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,” and in two [of them], it is written, “And he shall slaughter it.” What does the verse teach? These are three exclusions, as it is implied by all of them: This is slaughtered in the [Temple] courtyard, and not another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:5.hebrew: מנין לרבות את העופות - שאין שחיטתן מפורשת בתורה. הכי גרסינן בתורת כהנים: "תלמוד לומר: ושחטו, ושחט אותו, ושחט אותו", והכי נמי גרסינן בסיפרי. ופירושא: חד לחיה, וחד לעופות, וחד לאיסור אכילה בדיעבד. ודקתני "מרבה אני את החיה", הכי קאמר: אי לא כתב קרא, איכא למימר: אתא לריבויא בדוחקא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:16:5.english: From where to include fowl - For their slaughter is not explicitly stated in the Torah. This is the reading in Torat Kohanim: “The verse states: ‘And he shall slaughter it,’ ‘and he shall slaughter it,’ and ‘and he shall slaughter it’”; and this is also the reading in the Sifrei. And its explanation is: One [verse is] for a wild animal, one is for fowl, and one is for the prohibition of eating [it] after the fact. And that which [the baraita] teaches: “I include the wild animal,” this is what it means to say: If Scripture had not written [a verse], one could say [that] it comes to be included [only] with difficulty.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:1:1.hebrew: מוקצה - בהמה שהוקצה לתקרובת ע"ז אסורה לגבוה, כדאמר בתמורה (דף כח.): "מן הבהמה" — להוציא את הרובע ונרבע, "מן הבקר" — להוציא את הנעבד, "מן הצאן" — להוציא את המוקצה. נעבד — שהשתחוה לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:1:1.english: Set aside - An animal that was set aside for an offering to idol worship is forbidden to the Most High, as [the Gemara] says in Temurah (28a): "From the animal" — to exclude an animal that copulated with a person and [an animal that] was copulated with; "from the herd" — to exclude the worshipped [animal]; "from the flock" — to exclude the set-aside [animal]. "Worshipped" — [an animal] that one bowed down to.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:2:1.hebrew: רובע ונרבע בעדים - דבני סקילה נינהו, דכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:ט״ז): והרגת את האשה ואת הבהמה, ונרבע — דכתיב (שם): ואת הבהמה תהרוגו. וילפינן לעיל (קידושין דף נו:): משנגמר דינו נאסר, ואפילו שחטו. ולהכי נקט בעדים, דאינו נסקל בעד אחד, דאמר מר (בב"ק דף מד:): כמיתת הבעלים, כך מיתת השור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:2:1.english: An animal that copulated or was copulated with, in the presence of witnesses - For they are subject to stoning, as it is written: “And you shall kill the woman and the beast” (Leviticus 20:16); and [with regard to] an animal that was copulated with, as it is written: “And you shall kill the beast” (ibid. 20:15). And we learned above (Kiddushin 56b) [that] once its verdict is finalized, it is forbidden [for benefit], and even if one slaughtered it. And for this reason [Rabbi Yirmeya] specified “in the presence of witnesses,” because it is not stoned on the basis of a single witness, as the Master said (Bava Kamma 44b): Just as the death of the owners [requires two witnesses], so is the death of the ox.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:3:1.english: Jaffa - Its wall is on the sea.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:3:2.hebrew: בגבת - חומתה על המדבר, ורחמנא אמר: ״שדה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:3:2.english: In Gevat - Its wall is on the wilderness, and the Merciful One said: “Field.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:3:3.hebrew: שעומד בתוך העיר ויזרקנה חוץ לחומה - מדכתיב: "ושלח את הצפור החיה אל מחוץ לעיר", מכלל דעומד בעיר ומשלחה אל החוץ. דאי בעומד חוץ לעיר, מאי "ושלח אל מחוץ לעיר" איכא? הא מעיקרא, קודם שילוח, נמי התם קיימא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:3:3.english: That he stands inside the city and throws it outside the wall - Since it is written: “And he shall let go the living bird out of the city” (Leviticus 14:53), [this] implies that he stands in the city and sends it outside. For if [it referred to one who] stands outside the city, what [meaning of] “and he shall let go out of the city” is there? Behold, from the outset, prior to the sending forth, it was also standing there!

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:5:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - סברא הוא שהמשולחת מותרת, דלא אמרה התורה "שלח" לתקלה — שתהא למכשול עון, וילכדנה אדם ויאכלנה. וקרא דאמרן לעיל "לרבות את המשולחת", אסמכתא בעלמא היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:5:1.english: Rava says - It is [a matter of] logical reasoning that the sent-away [bird] is permitted, as the Torah did not say “let go” for a stumbling block — that it should be an obstacle [leading to] sin, and a person would trap it and eat it. And the verse that we cited above, “to include the sent-away [bird],” is a mere support.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:6:1.hebrew: אמר קרא קדש יהיה - חסר וי"ו כתיב, למידרש ביה: קודש הוא. וזה א' מן השלשה עשר במסורת חסרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:6:1.english: The verse states: “He shall be holy” - It is written missing a vav, in order to expound from it [that] it is holy; and this is one of the thirteen [occurrences] in the Masorah [written] deficient.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:6:2.hebrew: אמר קרא קדש יהיה - חסר וי"ו כתיב, למידרש ביה: קודש הוא. וזה א' מן השלשה עשר במסורת חסרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:6:2.english: The verse states: “He shall be holy” - It is written lacking a vav, to expound from it: “It is holy.” And this is one of the thirteen [occurrences] in the Masorah [written] defectively.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:7:1.hebrew: קדוש קרינן - להכי קרינן "קדוש" — למעוטי דמיו, שאין דין קדושה עליו. "קודש" משמע שם קדושה; "קדוש" משמע: הוא קדוש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:7:1.english: We read “holy” [kadosh] - It is for this [reason] that we read “kadosh”: to exclude its [redemption] money, so that the status of sanctity does not apply to it. “Kodesh” implies the designation of sanctity, [whereas] “kadosh” implies [that] it [itself] is holy.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:8:1.hebrew: פלוגתא דר' יהודה ור' שמעון - בבכורות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:8:1.english: The dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon - [Is] in Bekhorot.

Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:8:2.hebrew: לאחר עריפה ודברי הכל - דאמר התם: ומודה רבי שמעון לאחר עריפה שהוא אסור, וגמר עריפה עריפה מעגלה ערופה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 57b:8:2.english: After [its] neck has been broken, and everyone agrees - For it is stated there: And Rabbi Shimon concedes after [its] neck has been broken that it is forbidden, and he derives [via the verbal analogy of] “breaking the neck” [and] “breaking the neck” from the heifer whose neck is broken.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:11:1.hebrew: מה שלי בשלך אסור - פי' בקונטרס: אסור בהנאה, לפי שאין להם מי יתירם; דכיון דהוקדשו, אינן יכולין להיות מותרים אלא ע"י זריקה מתרת בקדשים, ואלו שנשחטו בחוץ אין נזרקין. והקשה הר"מ: דכמו כן מצינו שזריקה מוציאה מידי מעילה, ואפילו הכי אמרינן (מעילה דף יב.): קדשים שמתו יצאו מידי מעילה, ואע"ג שלא נזרק הדם; וכמו כן נאמר שהשחיטה תוציא מידי איסור אבר מן החי, ויהיו מותרים באכילה! לפיכך פירש הר"ם: "מה שלי בשלך אסור" — ואין להם תורת קדשים לעלות למזבח לפטור הבעלים; "אף שלך בשלי" — לא היה להם תורת חולין, ולא חזו להתרה דשייך בהו, דהיינו אכילה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:11:1.english: "Just as Mine in yours is forbidden" - The Kuntres explains: It is forbidden for [any] benefit, because they have nothing to permit them. For since they were consecrated, they cannot become permitted except through [blood] sprinkling, [which] permits with regard to consecrated items, and these that were slaughtered outside [the Temple courtyard] do not have [their blood] sprinkled. And the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir] questioned [this]: For we likewise find that sprinkling removes [consecrated meat] from [the laws of] me’ilah [misappropriation of consecrated property], and even so, we say (Meilah 12a): "Consecrated animals that died have exited [the laws of] me’ilah," even though the blood was not sprinkled; and likewise let us say [here] that the slaughter should remove [the meat] from the prohibition of a limb from a living animal [eiver min haḥai], and they should be permitted for consumption! Therefore, the Ram explained: "Just as Mine in yours is forbidden" — and [this means that] they do not have the legal status of consecrated items to ascend upon the altar [and] to exempt the owners [from their obligation]; "so too, yours in Mine" — they do not have the legal status of non-sacred [animals], and are not fit for the permit that pertains to them, which is eating.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:16:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר ושחטו ושחט אותו ושחט אותו - פי' בקונטרס: דתלתי קראי צריכי — חד לחיה, וחד לעופות, וחד לאיסור אכילה בדיעבד, כדמפרש גמרא: "אם אינו ענין לשחיטה, תניהו לאכילה"; דלבעלי מומין לא איצטריך קרא אף לשחיטה, כדמפרש טעמא: "שהרי הוא מין הכשר", והספר רוצה להביאו מסברא ולא צריך קרא. אע"ג דבחיה נמי קאמר: "מרבה אני את החיה, שישנה בשחיטה כבהמה", משמע דבלאו קרא מייתי לה — ויש לומר דה"ק: "מרבה אני את החיה" — בדוחק, אי לאו קרא; אבל כיון דאיכא קרא, נוקי בה קרא. אבל בעלי מומין יותר שוין, שהן מין הכשר וישנו בשחיטה. עוד י"ל: ת"ל "ושחטו ושחט אותו ושחט אותו", דמשמע דמצריך ג' קראי: חד לבעלי מומין, וחד לחיה, וחד לעופות. ואיסור אכילה בדיעבד נפקי לה מקרא דתמימים; דכי היכי דנפקא לן דאסירי לאכול תמימים מ"וזבחת ואכלת", כמו כן נמי אסור הני, מאחר דנפקא לן דאסור לשוחטן בעזרה, דנאמר דקרא ד"מה שאתה זובח" קאי אכולהו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:16:1.english: "The verse states: 'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it'" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that three verses are needed: one for a non-domesticated animal, one for fowl, and one for the prohibition of consumption after the fact, as the Gemara explains: "If it is not applicable to slaughter, apply it to consumption"; for regarding blemished animals, a verse was not necessary even for slaughter, as it explains the reason: "Since it is of the fit species," and the book seeks to derive it through logical reasoning and does not need a verse. Even though regarding a non-domesticated animal as well it states, "I include the non-domesticated animal since it is [subject to] slaughter like a domesticated animal," which implies that it derives it without a verse, one can say that this is what it means: "I include the non-domesticated animal" — [only] with difficulty, were there no verse; but since there is a verse, let us establish the verse for it. However, blemished animals are more similar [to unblemished offerings], as they are of the fit species and are subject to slaughter. Furthermore, it can be said: [When the baraita says,] "The verse states: 'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,'" this implies that it requires three verses: one for blemished animals, one for a non-domesticated animal, and one for fowl. And the prohibition of consumption after the fact is derived from the verse regarding unblemished animals; for just as we derive that unblemished animals are forbidden to be eaten from "and you shall slaughter... and you shall eat," so too these are also forbidden, once we have derived that it is forbidden to slaughter them in the Temple courtyard, as we say that the verse of "that which you slaughter" applies to all of them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:2:1.hebrew: הרי רובע ונרבע בעדים דבעלי חיים נינהו ואסירי - להכי נקט עדים, דאי על פי עד אחד או על פי בעלים — אינם אסורין להדיוט. ואם תאמר: לפי' ר"ת, דמפרש דשור הנסקל שרי בהנאה כל זמן שהוא חי, אלא עד אחר הסקילה, וכן נמי קאמר ברובע ונרבע — אם כן, קשה מהכא: דמאי קאמר "דבעלי חיים אסירי", דמשמע אסורין בהנאה אף מחיים? ולפי שיטתו, לא נזכר כאן הנאה כלל, אלא ה"פ: "לא מצינו בעלי חיים דאסירי" — כלומר, שהזהיר הכתוב שלא לשוחטו כדי לאכול הבשר; ופריך: "הרי רובע ונרבע דבעלי חיים נינהו", ולא הזהיר הכתוב אלא לשוחטן כדי לאכול הבשר, אבל ליהנות מהם כל זמן שהם חיים — ודאי מותר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:2:1.english: "Behold, an animal that copulated and one that was copulated with in the presence of witnesses, which are living creatures and are forbidden" - For this reason it specified [that it was in the presence of] witnesses, for if [it were established] on the basis of a single witness or on the basis of the owner['s admission], they are not forbidden to an ordinary person. And if you say: According to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, who explains that an ox that is to be stoned is permitted for benefit as long as it is alive, [and is not forbidden] until after the stoning, and he likewise says so regarding an animal that copulated and one that was copulated with — if so, it is difficult from here: for why does it say, "for they are living creatures and are forbidden," which implies that they are forbidden for benefit even during their lifetime? Yet according to his approach, [the prohibition against deriving] benefit is not mentioned here at all; rather, this is its explanation: "We have not found living creatures that are forbidden" — that is to say, where Scripture forbade slaughtering it in order to eat the meat; and it objects: "Behold, an animal that copulated and one that was copulated with, which are living creatures" — and [there too] Scripture only forbade slaughtering them in order to eat the meat, but deriving benefit from them as long as they are alive is certainly permitted.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:3:1.hebrew: כל שעומד תוך העיר ויזרקנה חוץ לחומה - פי' הקונטרס: דבשדה לא מהני שילוח, דבעינן "ושלח על פני השדה". וקשה: שהרי מצורע היה ונטהר חוץ לעיר, שהרי אסור ליכנס לפנים מן החומה! וי"ל: דשמא אחר כפרה היה הכהן נושאה — או הוא או שלוחו — לעיר, ומשלחה חוץ לעיר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 57b:3:1.english: "Any [manner in which] he stands inside the city and throws it outside the wall" - Rashi explains that [standing] in the field, sending [the bird] forth is not effective, as we require [fulfillment of the verse]: "And he shall let go... into the open field" [implying sending it from the city to the field]. And this is difficult, for the leper was [located] and purified outside the city, as he is forbidden to enter inside the wall! And one can say that perhaps after the atonement, the priest would carry it—either he or his agent—into the city, and send it forth outside the city.
